title: CS expansion sprint: templates + renewal tracker
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working sprint doc for Customer Success (CS) to run targeted expansion plays across three product levers: Dedicated upgrades, Private deployments, and Premium SLA add-ons. It contains: a lightweight QBR template focused on expansion signals, a living renewal tracker table (text first, spreadsheet later), 3 concise play flows with trigger logic, sample outreach sequences, and handoff checklists for Solutions/AE. Draft — intentionally informal; use and iterate in the upcoming expansion sprints.

Goals and success criteria (for a 6-week sprint):
- Convert 8–12 identified accounts to next-stage expansion conversations
- Book technical scoping for 4 Private deployment candidates
- Close at least 2 Dedicated upgrade deals (pilot -> reserved capacity)
- Add SLA pilots to 3 large accounts to accelerate premium renewals
- Measure: #opps created, pipeline $ value, demo/scoping bookings, conversion rate from scoping -> contract

KPI dashboard (minimum signals to update weekly):
- Active renewal cohort ARR (30–180 days out)
- Accounts using >50% of host concurrency (good Dedicated upsell candidate)
- Accounts with PII/compliance reqs flagged in security review (Private deploy candidate)
- Error/retry spike frequency + token spend variance (SLA upsell signal)

QBR template (compact, 30–40 minutes, expansion-focused)
1) Pre-read (send 3 days prior): one-pager with usage trends, cost per 1K tokens, latency percentiles, top 3 API routes, known incidents last 90 days.
2) Attendees: CS lead, customer engineering lead, product owner, finance buyer (if >$100k ARR).
3) Agenda: 
   - 5m: Wins & health (CS opens with 2–3 positive outcomes)
   - 10m: Usage & efficiency (call out growth patterns, peak windows)
   - 10m: Risk & incidents (brief RCA if needed)
   - 10m: Opportunities & recommended next steps (dedicated/private/SLA options)
   - 5m: Commitments & owner alignment (agree next actions + dates)
4) Expansion callouts (one slide):
   - Dedicated candidate? (Yes if sustained high concurrency or 99th pct latency degradation)
   - Private candidate? (Yes if procurement/compliance ask OR >$X ARR and sensitive data)
   - SLA candidate? (Yes if customer requires 99.9/99.95 SLOs for uptime or recovery time)
5) Template deliverables after QBR: scoped SOW request, technical scoping ticket, pricing sketch, and date for follow-up

Renewal tracker (text table — migrate to sheet later):
Columns: Account | ARR | Renewal window | CS owner | Primary technical contact | Expansion hypothesis | Trigger(s) | Current stage | Next action | Last contact
Sample rows:
- Acme Retail | $220,000 | 2026-04-15 | Aisha P. | Simon H. (Eng) | Move to Dedicated for predictable throughput | sustained 95th pct latency spikes | qualification | book infra scoping call by 2026-02-28 | 2026-02-10
- NovaHealth | $380,000 | 2026-06-01 | Marco R. | Dr. Liu (Sec) | Private deploy for HIPAA scope + HSM KMS | Security questionnaire flagged; compliance interest | solution scoping | produce architecture brief by 2026-03-10 | 2026-02-17
- FinLift | $95,000 | 2026-03-05 | Priya M. | Raj P. (Prod) | Premium SLA for guaranteed fallback & priority support | recent spike in incident impact | renewal discussion | propose SLA pilot by 2026-02-25 | 2026-02-12

Play 1: Dedicated upgrade (concise operational play)
Trigger signals (any): sustained >75% reserved GPU utilization in hosted; recurring latency tail > target; customer expresses cost/throughput predictability need.
Step 0: Qualification checklist (CS):
  - Confirm avg tokens/day and peak tokens/min
  - Identify model(s) & sequence lengths
  - Confirm data sensitivity (affects Dedicated vs Private)
  - Finance: current spend run-rate and budget horizon
Step 1: Value snapshot (one-pager): show current token cost, projected unit cost on Dedicated, expected latency improvement, and risk reduction (fallback paths).
Step 2: Technical scoping call (solutions eng + customer eng): capture estimated GPU footprint, throughput targets, peak concurrency, and any custom routing needs. Open Jira ticket: SOL-DED-<acct>-YYYY
Step 3: Pricing sketch & next steps (CS + sales): propose commit bands (monthly/annual), optional burst credits, and onboarding timeline (4–6 weeks).
Step 4: Pilot -> reserved (if pilot): define guardrails, SLOs, and rollback plan. Post-commit: transition to onboarding checklist (see handoff).
Risks / objections & short counters:
  - "We don't want vendor lock-in" -> emphasize same API surface, ability to change model pins, and migration plan; quantify cost benefit.
  - "We can't commit budget now" -> suggest pilot or short-term reserved with opt-out at end of pilot.

Play 2: Private deployment (VPC / on-prem)
Trigger signals: procurement/compliance asks, legal/regulatory redlines, or >$500k ARRish with high-data-sensitivity.
Minimum qualification (CS + Security):
  - Data classification: PII/PHI?
  - Required regional isolation or on-prem?
  - Legal: required contracts and timelines
  - Infra: customer infra readiness (k8s, bare-metal, networking constraints)
Core steps:
  1) Triage call with Security and Solutions (collect requirements)
  2) Generate 'private-deploy scoping doc' (inventory of endpoints, expected load, latency SLOs, KMS requirements)
  3) Timeline & resources: show typical 8–12 week delivery for VPC onboarding, 12–20 for fully air-gapped on-prem packages
  4) Draft MSA addendum & compliance checklist with Legal
  5) Technical pilot (staged: dev sandbox -> prod cutover)
Deliverables: architecture brief, runbook for updates, triage escalation path, and customer sign-off for maintenance windows.
Common blockers and mitigation:
  - Procurement delays -> keep weekly legal sync + prioritize standard addenda templates
  - Network ops concerns -> early network call to exchange CIDR/IP, egress policies, and peering windows

Play 3: Premium SLA add-on
Why sell SLA? Reduces renewal churn, increases ACV, and buys urgency for enterprise legal cycles. Use when: revenue >$100k ARR and customer requires defined recovery/time-to-response.
SLA tiers (suggested):
  - Bronze: 99.8% uptime + 8 business hour P1 response
  - Silver: 99.9% uptime + 4 business hour P1 response + quarterly review
  - Gold: 99.95% uptime + 1 hour P1 response + monthly review + designated TAM
Quick ROI note: for a $250k ARR account, incremental price for Gold ~ 6–10% ACV depending on SLA credits and premium support overhead. Present as optional line item with pilot discount.
SLA pilot design:
  - 90-day pilot for Silver/Gold with readouts on latency, incident MTTR, and response times
  - Escalation matrix + named contacts from both sides
Contract notes: SLA credits cap, exclusion list (planned maintenance windows), and definitions for downtime. Run Legal pre-approval for any revenue-impacting credit terms.

Multi-channel outreach sequences (30-day sequence for mid-funnel accounts)
Day 0: Short value email (CS) — attach one-pager + proposed scoping window
Day 3: Technical nudge (Solutions) — ask for 30m scoping with 2 optional windows
Day 10: Executive note (CS manager/AE) — call out renewal window and recommended option
Day 18: Case study + ROI snapshot — share 2 similar-customer outcomes
Day 25: Final reminder + booking link (calendar)
Email template snippets (short):
- Subject: Quick scoping for performance & cost wins — 15 min?
- Body: "Simon — we saw steady growth in your peak usage and want to show a quick config that reduces 95th pct latency and lowers unit cost. 15 min scoping next Tue/Thu?"
- SLA upsell subject: "Proposal: 99.95% SLA pilot for FinLift — details inside"

Handoff checklist to AE / Solutions after qualification (one-liners):
- Completed scoping doc attached (yes/no)
- Estimated footprint & models listed
- Recommended product (Dedicated / Private / SLA) and justification
- Proposed pricing band and timeline
- Internal tickets opened: SOL-TECH, Legals, Billing
- Suggested POC dates + success criteria

Playbook maintenance and cadence:
- Update this doc after each closed loop with a short postmortem (what worked/unexpected objections).
- Weekly CS sync: highlight 5 hottest expansion opps and blockers.
- Monthly cross-functional review (CS + Solutions + Legal + Finance) for any recurring scoping patterns that merit a new SKU.

Appendix: quick objection handling cheat-sheet
- "We need on-prem entirely" -> qualify for hybrid (VPC first) unless regulatory demands full air-gap; escalate to Solutions for architecture alternatives
- "We can’t sign off on long commit" -> offer short pilot with minimum commit + option to convert to reserved with credit
- "Support coverage questions" -> map their needs to SLA tiers and share TAM availability for Gold

Next actions (owner & due dates):
- Move tracker into a shared sheet and populate with top-25 renewal accounts (Aisha) — due 2026-02-28
- Run first expansion QBR template with Acme Retail and NovaHealth; capture scoping notes (Marco + Priya) — QBRs scheduled week of 2026-03-08
- Prepare a pricing sketch template for Dedicated (Finance + Sales) — draft due 2026-03-03

Notes & open questions:
- Do we want fixed packaged SKUs for Dedicated vs purely custom pricing? (Discuss Finance + Sales)
- What is the minimum ARR threshold for approving Private deployment requests without exec sign-off? (suggest $400k)

End of doc — iterate here.
